newsitem.title: USA: Aviation panel calls for new security measures.
newsitem.headline: Aviation panel calls for new security measures.

text.p: A federal aviation panel on Thursday called for measures ranging from new passenger and baggage screening to tighter cargo security as a way to combat airline and airport terrorism.
It put the cost at $9.9 billion over the next 10 years, but said government funds should be provided to cover spending by airlines, airports and others in the aviation system.

The panel's recommendations were made to the Aviation Security Advisory Committee, formed by the Federal Aviation Administration to update its "baseline" security standard that had been set some 20 years ago primarily to fight hijackings.

Its recommendations in many cases are refinements to measures in the 1996 federal aviation bill or being considered by a special commission formed after the explosion of TWA flight 800 off New York on July 17.

The cause of the TWA crash, which killed all 230 people on board, has not yet been determined, but investigators have recently swung away from believing a bomb may have destroyed the plane to the possibility the cause was mechanical failure.
Although the FAA panel was formed before the crash, it said that the evolving threat of terrorism and the increased use of explosives required that new security standards be set.
It said its recommendations were based most importantly on effectiveness rather than cost, but that no "unfunded" mandates would be imposed on the aviation industry.
The panel added that its recommendations were focused on "terrorist attacks related to weapons and explosives introduced into the civil aviation system."
And, it added, "Terrorism is a national security issue, not an air carrier or airport issue."

In addition to new passenger, baggage and cargo screening, the panel called for tighter scrutiny of all aviation industry workers, authority to search flights arriving from airports designated as high risk, increased use of bomb-sniffing dogs and the speedy installation of explosives detection devices.
